findings.quote: The majority age for the older citizenship-election cases was $21$. Republic Act $6809$ later lowered the general majority age to $18$. Do not use today's age to decide when someone born before $1973$ reached adulthood.
findings.problem: This treats all pre-1973 births as reaching majority at 21. Someone born in 1972 reached 18 after RA 6809 lowered majority in 1989. The applicable majority age depends on when adulthood was reached, not simply on being born before 1973. The supplied brief does not support this blanket historical instruction.

findings.quote: The majority age for the older citizenship-election cases was $21$. Republic Act $6809$ later lowered the general majority age to $18$. Do not use today's age to decide when someone born before $1973$ reached adulthood.
findings.problem: The historical-election condition is misstated as a single age rule for everyone born before 1973. It must distinguish people who reached adulthood before and after RA 6809 changed the majority age. Otherwise students are told to apply the wrong age to part of the covered group.
